View package dependencies as a flow diagram

Source: R/15_flow_view_package_deps.R
flow_view_package_deps.Rd

Creates a dependency graph showing how packages depend on each other. The function recursively resolves package dependencies and generates a nomnoml diagram.

flow_view_package_deps(
  pkg,
  db = NULL,
  demote_nodep = FALSE,
  base = FALSE,
  out = NULL
)

Arguments

pkg

Character vector of package names to analyze

db

A matrix of package metadata as returned by utils::available.packages(), passed to tools::package_dependencies(). By default the package index of the repositories set in getOption("repos") is used, which requires an internet connection.

demote_nodep

Logical. If TRUE, packages with no dependencies are shown with a "+" prefix in the diagram

base

Logical. If FALSE (default), base packages are excluded from the dependency graph

out

Output specification. If NULL, returns a flow_diagram object. Can be "html", "png", "pdf", etc. for file output, or "data" to return the dependency data

Value

A flow_diagram object containing the dependency graph, or the output path if out is specified

Examples

# a toy package database, to run offline
db <- cbind(
  Package = c("pkgA", "pkgB", "pkgC"),
  Depends = c("R (>= 4.0)", NA, NA),
  Imports = c("pkgB, utils", "pkgC", NA),
  LinkingTo = NA
)
flow_view_package_deps("pkgA", db = db)

# Include base packages
flow_view_package_deps("pkgA", db = db, base = TRUE)

# Show packages with no dependencies inside their dependent's box
flow_view_package_deps("pkgA", db = db, demote_nodep = TRUE)

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# Use the CRAN package index
flow_view_package_deps("dplyr")
flow_view_package_deps(c("dplyr", "ggplot2"))
}
